# Create and manage an HCP account

Learn how to create an HCP account, manage your account settings, and remove your account.

## Overview

An HCP account gives you access to HCP services and products, including HCP Terraform, and HashiCorp community resources such as tutorials and the Discuss forums. You can create an account using email and password, GitHub, or IBMid. After creating an account, you can manage your sign-in methods, password, and multi-factor authentication (MFA) from your account settings.

<Warning>

Email and password sign-in is being removed from HCP on 31 January 2027. Before that date, add IBMid or GitHub as a sign-in method for your account. If you use SAML SSO, you must also update the SSO Sign-On URL in your identity provider. Refer to [Set up SAML SSO](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/sso/setup/saml) for instructions.

</Warning>

### Account geography

HCP requires separate accounts for the global and European geographies to meet data residency requirements. To create a global HCP account, sign up on [the HCP portal](https://portal.cloud.hashicorp.com/). To create an HCP Europe account, sign up on [the HCP Europe portal](https://portal.cloud.eu.hashicorp.com/). Refer to [HCP Europe](/hcp/docs/hcp/europe) for more information.

### HashiCorp products and resources

You can also use your HCP credentials to sign in to the following HashiCorp products and educational resources:

- [HCP Terraform](https://cloud.hashicorp.com/products/terraform): Refer to the [HCP Terraform documentation](/terraform/cloud-docs/users-teams-organizations/users#log-in-with-your-hcp-account) to learn how to log in with your HCP credentials.
- [Tutorials](/hcp/tutorials): Step-by-step tutorials to learn HCP and other HashiCorp products
- [Discuss](https://discuss.hashicorp.com): Discussion forums where you can ask questions and product announcements
- [HashiConf virtual events](https://hashiconf.com): Resources for HashiCorp's bi-annual conference

## Requirements

Only users who signed up for HCP with their email and password or with GitHub can [remove their accounts](#remove-your-account) in the HCP UI. SSO users, including SCIM-provisioned users, cannot remove their own accounts from the portal. If you authenticate using SSO, contact your organization administrator so that they can de-provision your account through your identity provider.

If your organization uses SSO, HashiCorp recommends maintaining at least one non-SSO user with administrative access. If all non-SSO administrative users are removed and SSO is later disabled, no local user may have sufficient permissions to administer the organization. Refer to [Single sign-on (SSO) overview](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/sso) for more information.


## Sign in with IBMid

You can use an IBMid to sign in to HCP. IBMid lets you use the same account you use with other IBM products and is required to open support cases with IBM.

If you do not have an IBMid, create one at [ibm.com/account/reg/signup](https://www.ibm.com/account/reg/signup).

### Add your IBMid to your HCP account

The result of signing in with IBMid for the first time depends on whether your IBMid email matches your HCP account email, and which sign-in methods your HCP account currently uses. To check your sign-in methods, go to **Account settings** and review the **Sign-in method** setting.

#### Email and password sign-in

If your IBMid email matches your HCP account email, HCP automatically recognizes your IBMid as a sign-in method for your existing account. You can sign in with either IBMid or email and password and have the same access. Your organization memberships, roles, and resource access are unchanged.

If your IBMid email is different from your HCP account email, IBMid creates a new, separate HCP account. Follow the steps in [Sign in with a different email address](#sign-in-with-a-different-email-address) to grant your IBMid access to your existing organization.

#### GitHub-only sign-in

If your HCP account uses GitHub sign-in only, signing in with IBMid always creates a new, separate HCP account, regardless of email address. This applies even when you use your GitHub account to sign in to IBMid, because that credential is for IBMid only and does not connect to your HCP GitHub authentication. HCP treats your IBMid and your GitHub login as two separate identities.

Follow the steps in [Sign in with a different email address](#sign-in-with-a-different-email-address) to grant your IBMid access to your existing organization.

#### GitHub and email sign-in

If your IBMid email matches your HCP account email, HCP automatically recognizes your IBMid as a sign-in method for your existing account. You can sign in with IBMid, GitHub, or email and password and have the same access.

If your IBMid email is different from your HCP account email, IBMid creates a new, separate HCP account. Follow the steps in [Sign in with a different email address](#sign-in-with-a-different-email-address) to grant your IBMid access to your existing organization.

### Sign in with a different email address

If signing in with IBMid creates a separate HCP account because the email addresses do not match, complete the following steps to grant your IBMid access to your existing organization.

1. Sign in to HCP with IBMid. HCP creates a separate account for this IBMid.
1. Sign out, then sign back in using your existing sign-in method.
1. Invite your IBMid account as a new member of your HCP organization and assign the appropriate permissions. Refer to [Invite users to an organization](/hcp/docs/hcp/admin/users#invite-users).
1. Optionally, remove your old account from HCP if you prefer to sign in with a single account.

After adding IBMid to your account, you can continue to sign in with email and password until 31 January 2027. Start signing in with IBMid before that date.

## Sign in with GitHub

You can use a GitHub account to sign in to HCP. The steps depend on whether your GitHub account email matches your HCP account email. 

### Sign in when email addresses match

At the HCP login screen, click the **GitHub** sign-in option. HCP automatically recognizes the matching email and adds GitHub as a sign-in method for your existing account. Your organization memberships, roles, and resource access are unchanged.

### Sign in with a different email address

Signing in with GitHub creates a new, separate HCP account. Complete the following steps to grant your GitHub account access to your existing organization:

1. Sign out of HCP, then sign back in with your existing method.
1. Invite your GitHub account as a new member of your HCP organization and assign the appropriate permissions. Refer to [Invite users to an organization](/hcp/docs/hcp/admin/users#invite-users).

### Sign in without an existing GitHub account

Complete the following steps to create a GitHub account and sign in to HCP:

1. Create a GitHub account at [github.com/signup](https://github.com/signup) using the same email address as your HCP account.
1. Sign in to HCP using the **GitHub** option.

If you want a single identity for HCP, consider using an IBMid that authenticates with GitHub. IBMid gives you access to IBM support cases while letting you use GitHub to sign in.

When HashiCorp publishes an update to the HashiCorp GitHub application, GitHub may ask you to reauthorize the application, even if you previously authorized it to sign in with your GitHub account.

## Manage account settings

You can review your account settings, change your password, manage email preferences, and enable multi-factor authentication (MFA) from your account settings screen.

Choose **Account settings** from your user profile menu to review basic information about your account.

Click **Security** in the sidebar to access additional features. You can perform the following actions on the **Security** screen:

- Click **Send password reset email** to initiate the process of changing your password. Follow the instructions in the email to proceed.

- Click **Enable MFA** to begin setting up MFA. Refer to the [Multi-factor authentication](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/mfa) documentation for next steps.

## Remove your account

You can remove your HashiCorp account from HCP, end your active sessions, and delete data associated with HCP. If you use your HashiCorp account to sign in to HCP Terraform, removing your account also removes your access to HCP Terraform. To regain access, sign in again with the same credentials or reset your password to recreate your HCP account.

<Warning>

Account removal cannot be undone. HCP immediately removes your access to organizations, projects, and resources associated with your account.

</Warning>

### Resolve ownership dependencies

Before removing your account, HCP performs an automated pre-flight check and blocks removal if you are the owner of one or more HCP organizations. You must resolve all ownership dependencies before your account can be removed.

To resolve an ownership block, complete one of the following actions for each organization you own:

- Assign the owner role to another user in the organization. Refer to [Access management](/hcp/docs/hcp/iam/access-management) for instructions.
- Complete the organization deletion checklist and delete the organization. Refer to [Delete an organization](/hcp/docs/hcp/admin/orgs#delete-an-organization) for instructions.

### Remove your account

After completing the preflight checks and resolving any ownership dependency blocks, complete the following steps to remove your account:

1. From your user profile menu, choose **Account settings**.
1. In the **Remove account** section, click **Remove my account**.
1. If your account is not eligible for removal, HCP prompts you with actions to take before you can proceed. Resolve any blocking conditions, and then repeat this procedure.
1. In the confirmation dialog, type `REMOVE` to confirm, then click **Remove my account**.

Your account is removed from HCP and you are redirected to the HCP sign-in page.
